title: In vivo passive lumbar flexion stiffness (low/transition/high zone slopes), side-lying, before and after 1-2 h of sitting
condition: passive (lumbar ES < 5% MVC); baseline and after prolonged sitting

quantity.name: passive flexion moment-angle zone slopes
quantity.definition: moment about L4-L5 (force x perpendicular distance from cradle force application to L4-L5) vs lumbar flexion angle (Isotrak source over sacrum, sensor over L1 spinous process) normalised to the max angle of the first trial (Trial 1a); 6th-order polynomial fit differentiated to find low and high breakpoints; slopes of linear fits in the low, transition and high zones
quantity.unit: Nm per % of Trial-1a max flexion

source.authors: Beach TAC, Parkinson RJ, Stothart JP, Callaghan JP

protocol.summary: Frictionless jig (McGill type): right side-lying, lower body strapped to a fixed platform, upper body strapped to a floating cradle on nylon ball bearings, arms folded around a column on the cradle; ASIS aligned for repeatability. Experimenter pushed the top of the cradle into flexion until voluntary end range; trials with ES > 5% MVC repeated; 3 trials per session; sessions before and after each hour of seated deskwork (stool, no back support).
how_to_simulate: Model side-lying (no gravity in the sagittal plane), pelvis and lower limbs fixed, thorax/upper body free on a frictionless support
Set all muscle activations to zero (passive muscle force-length, ligaments, discs)
Flex the lumbar spine (L1 relative to sacrum) from neutral to the model's max flexion and compute the passive moment about L4-L5 (moment that must be applied to the upper body)
Normalise angle to max flexion, identify low/high breakpoints from the slope change and compare zone slopes with session 1 (baseline) values

subject_model.source: Table 1 (mean of the male and female group means; derived)

protocol.notes: Angle normalised to each subject's Trial-1a max passive flexion (absolute angles not tabulated). Breakpoint locations (Fig 3) and max flexion angles (Fig 5) not digitised. Watt 2022 reviewed this study (not in its quantitative synthesis).
